title: Multi-Step Scheming Detection Benchmark: Evaluating Monitors on Temporally Extended Misbehavior

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly addresses the core threat model of sophisticated scheming. If monitors fail on temporally distributed misbehavior, current benchmarks give false sense of security. This has immediate implications for how monitoring is evaluated and deployed.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Constructing realistic multi-step scheming scenarios requires significant domain expertise. Beginners would struggle to design scenarios that are both realistic and clearly malicious when viewed collectively. Implementing sliding-window monitors adds complexity beyond basic API calls.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires constructing 10-15 synthetic scenarios (substantial design effort), implementing three different monitor types, and labeling at two levels. Could be scoped down to 5 scenarios and 2 monitor types to fit 30 hours, but as stated it is ambitious.
